slides.1.question: Which legendary Portuguese red, founded in 1952, is declared only in the best vintages?
slides.1.explanation: Barca Velha was created by Ferreira in 1952 and, thanks to its rarity, top quality and high price, is one of Portugal's most legendary reds. It is declared only in the very best vintages, about 21 so far.
slides.2.question: In blind tasting, which aroma is the strongest clue to identifying Touriga Nacional?
slides.2.explanation: Violet is the most distinctive identifier of Touriga Nacional and is extremely rare in other grape varieties. Together with deep purple-black colour and high tannin, it forms the golden combination for identifying Touriga Nacional.
slides.3.question: After how many years in oak casks is Vintage Port bottled?
slides.3.explanation: Vintage Port spends only a short time, 2 years, in oak casks before bottling. Its complexity comes mainly from long ageing in bottle (usually 15–25 years). This is quite different from LBV (4–6 years in cask) and Tawny (many years in cask).
slides.4.question: What was the main reason for the poor quality of the 2003 Douro vintage?
slides.4.options.1: A European heatwave caused over-ripeness, high alcohol and insufficient acidity
slides.4.explanation: Europe experienced a historic heatwave in 2003, and Portugal was severely affected. Extreme heat made the grapes over-ripen quickly, with sugar accumulating rapidly (high alcohol) and acidity lost. It is a classic case of the impact of modern climate change on wine quality.
slides.5.question: What is the main reason for Vinho Verde's success in the US market?
slides.5.options.0: High alcohol, suited to American tastes
slides.5.options.1: Low alcohol, fresh lightly spritzy character and good value fit modern drinking trends
slides.5.options.2: It is the cheapest imported wine in the US
slides.5.explanation: Vinho Verde's success in the US market comes from several factors: low alcohol (8–11.5%) suits health awareness, its natural light spritz is fresh and appealing, and value is excellent (entry-level wines at US$8–15 far exceed others at the same price). These traits fit modern consumer trends perfectly.
slides.6.question: Which combination of factors is the core reason Madeira can age for centuries?
slides.6.options.0: The influence of special volcanic basalt soils
slides.6.options.1: Estufagem oxidation + high alcohol + high acidity
slides.6.options.2: The unique preserving effect of the island climate
slides.6.options.3: Sealed storage in stainless steel tanks
slides.6.explanation: The secret of Madeira's extreme longevity is triple protection: the Estufagem process has already fully oxidised the wine (so it will not evolve further into spoilage), high alcohol (17–22%) suppresses microbes, and high acidity maintains structure and vitality. Together these three factors create a unique, ageless wine.
slides.7.question: Which description of the Baga grape is the most accurate?
slides.7.options.0: Known for violet aromas and a smooth palate
slides.7.options.1: Mainly planted in the Douro, the core grape of Port
slides.7.options.2: High acidity and high tannin, tight when young, needs ageing to show its charm
slides.7.options.3: The most widely planted grape in Portugal
slides.7.explanation: Baga is the signature grape of Bairrada, known for some of the highest acidity and astringent tannin in the world. It is very tight and harsh when young, but with age can develop remarkable finesse and complexity. Its identifying feature is "acidity", an important clue when blind tasting Portuguese grapes.
slides.8.question: What is the main difference between Colheita and ordinary Tawny Port?
slides.8.options.0: Colheita is made only from Touriga Nacional
slides.8.options.1: Colheita is a single-vintage Tawny, aged in cask for at least 7 years, with the actual harvest year stated
slides.8.options.2: Colheita is more expensive than Vintage Port
slides.8.explanation: Colheita is a special form of Tawny Port. The key points are: (1) a single vintage (not a multi-year blend), (2) at least 7 years of ageing in oak casks, and (3) the actual harvest year stated on the label. This gives Colheita both the oxidative style of Tawny and the vintage character of Vintage Port.
slides.9.question: Which Portuguese region is considered a "beneficiary" in the face of climate change?
slides.9.explanation: Vinho Verde lies in north-west Portugal, most strongly influenced by the Atlantic, with relatively cool temperatures. As global warming makes the southern regions ever hotter, Vinho Verde's freshness is increasingly favoured by the market, and demand for top Alvarinho whites keeps rising.
slides.10.question: In Port collecting, why is "provenance" important?
slides.10.options.0: It determines the grape composition of the Port
slides.10.options.1: It is the key basis for assessing a wine's authenticity, storage history and market value
slides.10.options.2: It records the winemaking process of the Port
slides.10.explanation: Provenance (origin/source) is crucial in Port collecting and investing. It records the complete history of a bottle: where it was bought, how it was stored, and whether it comes from a well-known cellar or auction house. An old Port vintage with full provenance is worth far more than the same wine of unknown origin, and it is also an important safeguard against counterfeit old wines.
